'''''Diospyros vaccinioides''''', the '''small persimmon''', is a herbaceous plant, a member of the family [[Ebenaceae]]. This plant is mainly found in China and it is known to thrive in subtropical biomes.<ref name=POWO>{{Cite web |title=''Diospyros vaccinioides'' Lindl. {{!}} Plants of the World Online {{!}} Kew Science |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:323155-1 |access-date=2022-11-08 |website=Plants of the World Online |language=en}}</ref>

== Description ==
The fruit produced by this plant are classified as berries.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Small Persimmon data - Encyclopedia of Life |url=https://eol.org/pages/2892242/data |access-date=2022-11-22 |website=eol.org}}</ref>

== Distribution ==
[[File:楓港柿Diospyros vaccinioides 20210526094550 28.jpg|thumb|Growth size]]
It is native to [[Taiwan]].<ref name=":0" /> It is also native to China, specifically the Guangdong province, Hongkong, and Hainan.

== Taxonomy ==
It was named by [[John Lindley]], in ''Exot. Fl''. 2: t. 139. in 1825.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Diospyros vaccinioides Lindl. |url=https://www.gbif.org/species/7295838 |access-date=2022-11-22 |website=www.gbif.org |language=en}}</ref>
